prompt: Walk a small expression hierarchy (Num, Add, Mul, Neg) with recursion and pattern matching for instanceof: evaluate the tree, render it fully bracketed, and count its nodes.
explanation: The four records share one interface, so a single Expr reference can hold any node and each method must ask what it really is before it can go further. Recursion mirrors the shape of the data: a branch node asks the same method for its children and combines the answers, while Num is the base case that stops the descent. The final fall-through return handles null and any unknown Expr, which is what keeps the recursion total instead of throwing at the bottom of a tree.
hints: Handle Num first as the base case, then the branch nodes -- each branch calls the same method on its children.
'if (e instanceof Add add)' binds a typed variable, so add.left() and add.right() are available inside the block.
render builds its text from the rendered children, so bracketing falls out naturally: "(" + left + " + " + right + ")".
